claim: jump takes a 0-based STATEMENT index, and the in-game editor can only write a number there: a numeric target is the normal, editor-produced form and is not a mistake. It is only a promise about the statements above it -- insert or delete one statement and every literal target below it shifts. INFO: the editor gives no other option, so this is a reminder to re-check targets after editing, not a defect.
why: User m06173 (2026-11-03): a numeric line-number jump must not be reported as an error, because the vanilla editor can only use numeric jump targets -- the target is a number field, so every program touched in the editor carries numeric targets, and flagging them WARN turned a normal program into a wall of warnings (v0.23.3 review panel). LParser.java:117-125 records a label against the statement counter and :195-198 resolves a named jump to that 0-based number, which is exactly the literal jump N accepts, so both forms compile to the same instruction. A label is still the safer form for generated text (tools/msch.py writes code as text into logic data and the game resolves labels at load), but a number is what the editor writes and what a player can keep editing. The failure still worth catching is not "a number was used" but "the number points nowhere": jump-target-out-of-range (ERR) and unreachable-statement (WARN) carry that -- measured on out/jobs/43fe34c6557e3eeb.json (out/takeover-20261024/98-quality-analysis.md section 2), where jump 12 pointed one line past the label the author meant and four control shootp statements never ran. Downgraded WARN -> INFO on 2026-11-03 and consolidated to one finding per program.
